_comment: Situations inside adventures (Expansion 6 C.10; ADVENTURES.md §5.16 'Situations inside adventures'). A predicament with `inside` {step, route, chance} is never forged from a town's own roots: when an adventure's step of that kind is open and its person is in a peopled town, story/situations.for_step may make it that step's situation (its root kind 'adventure', `sit["adventure"]` and `sit["step"]`), its role 'asker' the step's person (bind 'given'). The op 'step' finishes the adventure's step (the witness tells the tale; the one who knows tells what it fears); 'key' gives the adventure a key. Its meetings are the scenes of scenes.inside.json. The words name no road, hour or beast's habit: the tale itself (the adventure's own words) says those.

silent_witness.name: A witness who will not speak

note: {kin_full} will not have {asker} telling the tale: the last one who frightened the market with it was fined by the reeve.
{kin} keeps {asker} indoors and does the talking at the door. Talk of the beast only brings it, to {kin_their} mind.
{kin_full} wants the whole thing forgotten, and {asker} will not cross {kin_them}.
magic_note: The spell did what words would not: {kin} stood aside.

label: Let {asker} speak. It is your neighbours who will die next.
say: ...Say it here, then, in the house. Not in the street.
Go on, then. Tell them. The gods help us all.
fail_say: You'll go off after it, and we'll be the ones left here when it comes. No.

label: For what you lost to it, and for the trouble. Let {asker} talk to me.
say: ...That's more than we lost. All right. Sit down, then.

label: Stand aside. I am not asking.
say: All right. All right. Talk to them, then, and be gone.
fail_say: You don't scare me half as much as that thing does. Get out.

label: Now. Tell me what you saw.
say: ...All right. I'll tell it the once, and then I never want to speak of it again.
Sit down. It takes a while, and I'll not tell it twice.

label: Meet me at the shrine after dark, where your {kin_kin} will not see.
say: ...After dark, then. By the shrine. If I'm not there, I'm not coming.
Tonight. Don't wait for me past the bell.
fail_say: I can't. I can't go behind my {kin_kin}'s back. Don't ask me.

line: {asker} told it all by the shrine in the dark, and was home again before {kin} missed {asker_them}. {kin} found out anyway.
Told, in secret. {kin} knows now, and has not spoken to {asker} since.
{asker} slipped out to tell it, and the whole street saw {asker_them} come back. There are hard words in that house now.
{asker} told it with {kin} glaring from the door. Neither of them will look at you in the street.
You had the tale, and {kin} had a fright. That house will not open its door to you again.
Told, because you made {kin} stand aside. {asker} shakes still when you pass.
{asker} told it all, and {kin} sat and listened, and did not stop {asker_them}. It was a weight off that house.
Told, with {kin}'s leave. {asker} pressed your hand at the door and said to come back when it is dead.
{asker} has said it out loud at last, and says that if you need a word spoken for you in {town}, you have only to ask.
{asker} could not carry it any longer and told it all to the priest. The priest sent it on to you, days late, and {asker} will not meet your eye.
In the end {asker} told it to the whole inn, drunk, and somebody remembered to send it on to you. {asker} wishes you had come.
{asker} told it without you in the end, at the well, while {kin} was out. Word of it reached you late, and {asker} blames you for the wait.

title: What {asker} saw
The one who will not tell
{asker}'s silence
stakes: what {asker} saw, and whether {kin} lets it be told
whether {asker} tells what came for them
plea: I saw it. Yes. But my {kin_kin} says if I tell it, it will come for me, or the reeve will. I can't. Not with my {kin_kin} the way things are.
Don't ask me here. My {kin_kin} won't have it talked of. Talk to {kin}, if you must. Or find another way.
I want to tell you. Every night I want to tell someone. But my {kin_kin} watches me, and says talk brings it.
first: {asker} saw it and lived, and will not tell it while {kin} forbids it.
{asker} knows what it looks like, and is keeping quiet for {kin}'s sake.
The one who saw it is {asker}. {kin} keeps {asker_them} from telling.
ask: They say you saw it. I need to know what you saw.
You saw it and lived. Will you tell me?
You saw it, didn't you? Tell me.
take: Then I'll find a way for you to tell it.
thanks: ...If you can make {kin} see sense, I'll tell you everything.
Be careful with {kin}. It's only fear, with {kin_them}.

hunter_holds_back.name: A hunter who will not hunt

note: {asker} swore over a grave never to go after it again, and means to keep the oath.
{asker} hunted it once, years ago, with a friend, and came back alone. Nothing more is said about the friend.
{asker} has a debt in {town} as well as an oath, and will not go off to be killed with either of them hanging.

label: What happened, the last time you went after it?
say: ...There were two of us. My friend and me. I came back. That's all there is.
We went after it, two of us, the winter I was young. I'm the one who came home.

label: Then come with me and finish it, for the friend you lost.
say: ...For them. All right. I'll show you the way, and I'll stand with you.
I've waited long enough. I'll come.
fail_say: You didn't see what it left of them. No. Find someone else.

label: The best hunter in {town}, sitting at home while it kills.
say: ...Damn you. Damn you. I'll come. And if it kills me, that's on you.
fail_say: Say what you like. I've heard worse from myself.

label: What do you owe, and to whom? I'll pay it, and you come.
say: ...That's every penny of it. Then there's nothing keeping me here. I'll fetch my bow.

line: {asker} will come, and will stand with you, and has not forgiven you for how you asked.
Shamed into it: {asker} has the bow strung and says nothing to you that does not need saying.
{asker} is coming with you, and spat in the dust when you left.
{asker}'s debt is paid and {asker_their} word is free. {asker} told you what it fears, and will stand with you.
Paid off and free: {asker} is waxing the bowstring and talking of the old hunt as if it were last week.
{asker} owes nobody in {town} now but you, and means to pay you in the only way a hunter can.
{asker} will come, for the friend who did not come home the last time, and told you what it fears.
{asker} has taken the old bow down from the wall. When you go after it, {asker} goes with you.
The oath is set aside, not broken. {asker} will stand with you at the end, and told you how it can be hurt.
{asker} kept the oath. The bow stays on the wall, and what {asker} knows of it stays unsaid.
Too late now: {asker} will not hear another word of it, and shuts the door when you pass.
The oath holds. {asker} sits at home and listens for news of you, and will not come.

title: The hunter's oath
Why {asker} will not hunt
The bow on the wall
stakes: whether {asker} breaks an old oath to hunt it with you
{asker}'s help, and what {asker} knows of it
the one hunter in {town} who has faced it and lived
plea: I know what it fears. I know where it lies up. And I'll not go near it again. I swore that, over a grave.
You want me out there with you. I know. Everyone wants that. I've my reasons, and one of them is buried.
Ask me anything but that. I'll not hunt it. I've done it once, and once was enough for a lifetime.
first: {asker} knows the beast better than anyone, and has sworn never to hunt it again.
{asker} could say what it fears and hunt it beside us, and will not.
The hunter is {asker}, who hunted it once, and something keeps {asker_them} from going again.
ask: They say you're the hunter here.
You know the country. Will you help me?
They tell me you've faced it before.
take: Then I'll find what keeps you here.
I'll not go without you, if I can help it.
thanks: ...You can try. You'll not be the first.
Talk all you like. I'll listen.
